title: Stock bar length
source: 12 m stock bars
rationale: Laps are added beyond this length.

title: Beam main-bar extension into each support, in bar diameters
source: typical anchorage
rationale: Bottom and top bars run the clear span plus this anchorage at both ends; 0 is the bare clear span.

title: What the schedule beam depth H is measured from
source: beam schedule (datum not printed on most Kuwait villa schedules)
rationale: TOTAL_DEPTH (B x H x L, the slab strip inside H) is the usual schedule convention; BELOW_SLAB (B x (H + t) x L) is the alternative and sets each beam's high end.

title: Beam bar lap length, in bar diameters
source: tension lap of beam bars
rationale: A bar longer than BAR_STOCK_LENGTH_M takes one lap per extra stock length.

title: Blinding where outlines overlap (beam strip on a footing, strips at a junction, footing projections)
source: one blinding layer under footings and beams
rationale: The blinding layer is cast once: its plan is the union of the footing outlines (+ projection) and the beam strips (band + projection each side), registered on the foundation plan by the columns landing in the footings, computed exactly by inclusion-exclusion of the convex outlines. An outline without a place (a footing by its label only, a curved band) is added whole. Without a registration the overlap is a coverage risk.

title: Blinding projection beyond the footing / ground beam, each side
source: ST7757 PDF p.13 (vector drawing, read visually; not reviewed): the second typical footing detail dimensions the plain concrete 10 beyond the footing face; every typical ground-beam section dimensions it 10 | 30 | 10 under the 30 cm beam
rationale: Printed on the typical details; to be confirmed by a person with the blinding thickness (RFI).

title: Blinding thickness when not printed (exposure only)
source: typical villa blinding
rationale: Only an exposure for UNRESOLVED blinding (never added to a total); blinding is measured only with a printed thickness (profile).

title: Blinding (plain concrete) thickness
source: ST7757 PDF p.13: '10cm Plain con.' in both typical footing details (OCR notes P13N01, P13N02 - each under a footing caption, read again visually) and a 10 cm hatched layer dimensioned under every typical ground-beam section; not reviewed by a person
rationale: The isolated-footing details print 10 cm plain concrete under 5 cm screed and a membrane; the ground-beam sections draw the same 10 cm layer. The screed and membrane are separate works, not blinding.

title: Members that sit on blinding
source: ST7757 PDF p.13: the plain-concrete layer is drawn and dimensioned (10 thick, 10 projection each side) under all four typical ground-beam sections and under both typical footing details
rationale: Both typical details show the layer.

title: Base reading of a continuous beam whose direction is ambiguous
source: both readings are computed
rationale: When the printed spans fit both directions equally, the reading with the larger bar mass is the base and the other sets the range (LOW confidence).

title: Continuous beam bottom bars beyond the far face of an interior support
source: ST7757 DXF CB typical details on SH03, SH05 and SH07: dimension text '7.5cm' at the bottom bar ends past the interior support
rationale: Printed on all three typicals; the end anchorage at an end support is not printed (BEAM_BAR_ANCHORAGE_D applies).

title: Continuous beam: margin by which one reading direction must fit better
source: sum of absolute span residuals
rationale: When the printed spans fit both directions, the reading whose summed residual is lower by at least this margin is taken; otherwise the direction is AMBIGUOUS and the bars carry both readings.

title: What a printed continuous-beam span length measures
source: design-model spans are support centre to support centre
rationale: AXIS compares support centres; CLEAR compares support faces. A project profile sets the printed basis where the schedule states it.

title: Continuous beam: tolerance between a drawn span and its printed length
source: printed spans are design-model lengths at 0.1 m resolution; drawn supports are column outlines
rationale: A drawn span matches its printed length within max(this, CB_SPAN_MATCH_TOL_REL x length). Every span of the sequence must match, in order.

title: Continuous beam: relative tolerance of a span match
source: as CB_SPAN_MATCH_TOL_M
rationale: The larger of the absolute and the relative tolerance applies to each span.

title: Continuous beam support (MID) bars: fraction of the span on each side
source: ST7757 DXF continuous-beam typical details on SH03, SH05 and SH07 (layer S-DIM.SCH): dimension texts '0.22 Ln', '0.22 Ln1', '0.22 Ln2' measured from the support face
rationale: Printed on all three typicals. The '0.3 Ln2' and '0.15L' dimensions bind to no support bar and are not used.

title: The span 'Ln' of the support-bar dimension
source: ST7757 DXF CB typical details: 'Ln' / 'Ln1' dimensions run support axis to support axis ('L' runs face to face)
rationale: The typical names its spans by their own dimension lines; Ln is axis to axis.

title: Untagged span collinear with a tagged span across a support
source: the schedule's printed span sequence of a continuous beam (continuous_beams.match)
rationale: An unlabelled span takes a continuous-beam mark only when it is one of the spans whose lengths match the schedule's printed span sequence. Alignment across a support is not evidence: such a span is UNRESOLVED, with the neighbour's section as an alternative and the schedule depths at its drawn width as the exposure. ALLOW is the M3 reading (every collinear span inherits); OFF leaves every untagged span unresolved.

title: Column main-bar lap per storey, in bar diameters
source: typical lap
rationale: Each storey's main bars run the storey height plus one lap.

title: Column drawn at another section than its schedule
source: drawn outline vs schedule storey band
rationale: Schedule as base; drawn as the alternative.

title: Footing bar ends
source: footing details
rationale: Straight between covers as base; 90 deg hooks at both ends as the high end.

title: Two footing types labelled at one footing with no outline
source: the two labelled schedule types
rationale: One physical footing carries two type labels and no outline settles it: it is quantified once, at the larger type (the conservative reading), with the smaller as the low bound. An RFI settles the type.

title: Footing mark with a schedule row but no outline found
source: footing schedule size of the labelled type
rationale: The label and its schedule type are certain; the outline is not found. The quantity is the schedule size, PROVISIONAL and LOW confidence, with a coverage-risk record; a second label next to an outline of the same type stays unresolved (never counted twice).

title: Footing drawn at another plan size than its schedule
source: drawn outline vs schedule row
rationale: Schedule as base; the drawn size is the alternative.

title: Footing outline with only a column mark
source: drawn outline vs footing schedule sizes
rationale: When exactly one footing type has the drawn plan size, the outline is that type (LOW confidence; an RFI confirms it).

title: Founding level below plot level (footing underside)
source: ST7757 general note (PDF, transcribed): excavation not less than 1.50 m below plot level
rationale: The printed minimum is the base and the low end; 2.00 m is a planning upper bound, not printed (RFI).

title: Depth range for an unmarked ground beam (exposure only)
source: villa ground beams
rationale: Used only for the UNRESOLVED exposure range; never in a total.

title: Floor build-up between the floor level and the top of an exterior ground beam
source: tiled floor on screed (finish + bedding)
rationale: The exterior depth runs from the slab level under the floor finish to the outer ground level; the finish thickness is not printed.

title: A perimeter ground beam takes the printed exterior detail
source: band side classification of the ground-beam plan (slab_engine.band_sides: a long side with no slab cell and no member beyond it)
rationale: A perimeter ground beam is only a candidate for the printed exterior detail (captioned for exterior walls): without architectural evidence the typical class section is the base and the exterior detail the high alternative. GB_EXTERIOR_EVIDENCE decides when the architecture is supplied.

title: Printed exterior ground-beam detail
source: ST7757 PDF p.13 'Ground Beams. for exterior walls' (labels 'Ground Floor slab level' and 'Outer Normal ground level'); bars from the detail-evidence document
rationale: The exterior detail spans from the ground-floor slab level to the outer ground level; width as the typical sections (30 cm).

title: Evidence that makes a perimeter ground beam exterior
source: arch_evidence.gb_exterior: the architectural ground-floor plan registered on the column outlines
rationale: ARCH_WALLS_REQUIRED: the exterior detail applies where the architecture draws a wall on a band with an outside side, at the floor level printed inside it; a band whose exterior depth would not be deeper than its class section is a source conflict (class section). PERIMETER is the M3 reading (every perimeter band).

title: Span length that selects a typical ground-beam class
source: typical section titles by span
rationale: Span conventionally means centre to centre; the clear-length class is the alternative.

title: Typical ground-beam sections by span (ST7757 p.13 titles)
source: ST7757.pdf p.13 typical ground-beam titles '< 2.5 m (30x30)', '< 5 m (30x40)', '> 5 m (30x60)' (vector glyphs; typed)
rationale: Read as exclusive span bands; exterior beams 'FOLLOW ARCH.' are not separated by the generic route (a known limit).

title: Ground-floor level above plot level
source: GF level +1.00 printed on the architectural section P7757 VE-AA-09 and on the ground-beam plan (+1.00)
rationale: The top of the exterior ground-beam detail is the ground-floor slab level.

title: Lintel bearing on each masonry jamb
source: lintel bearing on block walls
rationale: A column jamb takes no bearing; a masonry jamb this much.

title: Lintel schedule by opening width (cm)
source: ST7757 PDF p.13 'LINTEL SCHEDULE' (vector drawing, read visually, not reviewed): opening width 0-100 / 101-200 / 201-300 / 301-500 / 501-750 cm; size B x 20 / 20 / 30 / 40 / 55 (B = block wall width); bottom 2Ø12 / 2Ø14 / 3Ø16 / 3Ø18 / 4Ø18; top 2Ø10 / 2Ø12 / 3Ø14 / 3Ø14 / 3Ø14; stirrups 5Ø8/M
rationale: Bounds inclusive as printed; a width between two bands (e.g. 100.5 cm) is a schedule gap, never rounded into a band.

title: An opening with a structural beam over it
source: the head height against the beam soffit decides (elevations / sections)
rationale: Under a beam a separate lintel is needed only when the opening head is below the beam soffit; without head heights the opening is UNRESOLVED with the lintel volume as its exposure.

title: Foundation neck height when the founding level is not printed (exposure only)
source: typical villa necks
rationale: Only an exposure for an UNRESOLVED neck (never added to a total); a neck is measured only with the printed founding depth and neck top level of the project (profile).

title: Top of the foundation necks (GF level above plot level)
source: GF level +1.00 printed on the architectural section P7757 VE-AA-09 (the lift stops GF +1.00, 1F +5.50)
rationale: The neck runs from its footing top to the GF level, where the GF column starts (its height is GF +1.00 to 1F +5.50 = 4.50).

title: Outer ground level beside the building
source: levels printed outside the building on the ground-beam plan (SH08): +-0.00 and +0.15
rationale: The exterior detail runs down to the outer normal ground level; the plan prints +-0.00 and +0.15 outside the building, which set the range.

title: Beam cover to links
source: typical general notes
rationale: Overridden by a printed cover in the profile.

title: Column cover to ties
source: typical general notes
rationale: Overridden by a printed cover in the profile.

title: Footing cover
source: typical general notes
rationale: Overridden by a printed cover in the profile.

title: Code table for bends and hooks
source: engine.source.bbs_optimiser ACI 318-19 Tables 25.3.1 / 25.3.2 (not verified against a project document)
rationale: Diameter-aware bend diameters and hook tails; PROVISIONAL_CODE_METHOD.

title: A mark with two schedule rows
source: the schedule rows and the drawn width of the bound band
rationale: When one mark has two schedule rows and the drawn width matches exactly one of them, that row is the base; the other row gives the range. A drawn width that matches neither or both leaves the member UNRESOLVED.

title: Reading of a side-bar notation 'n Ø d / s'
source: typical-detail notation
rationale: The printed count is the base; bars at the printed spacing on each face over the section height give the high end.

title: A slab face's overlap with beam bands and column outlines
source: conservation: beams and columns own their plan area
rationale: A face whose polygon runs into a band or a column outline loses that area before its volume (never counted twice).

title: Directions of a slab mesh tag that does not say each way
source: slab bar tag without E.W.
rationale: A tag without E.W. covers one direction as base; both directions as the high end.

title: A sheet's single each-way mesh note applies to untagged panels
source: printed sheet note 'n Ø d /m E.W.'
rationale: One each-way mesh note on the sheet and no tag inside the panel: the note applies (scope confirmed by RFI).

title: Project default slab thickness (unless a panel prints its own)
source: ST7757 PDF p.8 general notes (vector glyphs, Arabic): a note naming slab / roof thickness with the value 16 cm, read by local Arabic OCR (unreviewed); the frozen S1 census records the same default as P8-N18 + P1-NOTE-A
rationale: Panels without their own thickness tag take the project default; the two 2F panels tagged 'T 18' keep 18 cm. To be confirmed by a person (RFI).

title: Untagged panels take the sheet's single printed thickness
source: every thickness tag on the sheet prints the same value
rationale: When all printed tags agree the sheet value applies to untagged panels.

title: Thickness range for a panel with no printed thickness (exposure only)
source: Kuwait villa slab range
rationale: Used only for the UNRESOLVED exposure range; never in a total.

title: Thickness of an untagged slab panel
source: a printed project default ('unless otherwise noted') governs every panel without its own tag
rationale: When the profile prints SLAB_PROJECT_DEFAULT_THICKNESS_M, untagged panels take it; one panel's local tag is never spread to the rest of its sheet. Without a printed default the sheet-uniform reading (SLAB_SHEET_UNIFORM_THICKNESS) applies.

title: Risers of a drawn stair run
source: a plan draws the tread nosings; the top riser arrives at the landing or floor
rationale: n drawn tread lines are n treads and n + 1 risers (LINES_PLUS_ONE); LINES reads each line as a riser. The riser height rise / risers must fall in 0.14 - 0.20 m, else the zone holds only part of the stair.

title: Stair waist when no section prints it (exposure only)
source: villa stair waists 15 - 20 cm
rationale: Only an exposure for an UNRESOLVED stair (never in a total); a printed waist (profile STAIR_WAIST_M) makes the stair PROVISIONAL.

title: Storey height 1F (floor to floor)
source: P7757 architectural section VE-AA-09 (printed floor-to-floor)
rationale: Typed from the printed section.

title: Storey height 2F (floor to floor)
source: P7757 architectural section VE-AA-09 (printed floor-to-floor)
rationale: Typed from the printed section.

title: Storey height GF (floor to floor)
source: P7757 architectural section VE-AA-09 (printed floor-to-floor)
rationale: Typed from the printed section.

title: Depth range for an untagged beam band with no schedule row at its width (exposure only)
source: villa beam depths
rationale: Used only for the UNRESOLVED exposure; when schedule rows exist at the band width their depth range is used instead.

title: Width of a beam drawn at another width than its schedule
source: drawn band width vs schedule row
rationale: The schedule is the design table; the drawn width is the alternative.
